strengths: Novel and well-motivated idea: using a compressed teacher KV-cache as a stepwise supervision signal for latent reasoning addresses a genuine gap (lack of direct supervision for continuous thoughts), and the observation that compressed caches lose token correspondence making standard distillation ill-posed is clearly articulated.

Consistent empirical gains: KA Va outperforms strong latent-reasoning baselines (CODI, PCCoT, Coconut, iCoT) across three backbones (Qwen2.5-0.5B, LLaMA3.2-1B/3B) and two training datasets, with particular improvements on natural-language traces (GSM8k-Aug-NL), which prior latent methods struggled with.

Thorough ablations: the paper isolates the contribution of the KV-matching loss and projection layer, studies loss type/coefficient sensitivity, eviction method choices (including a simple crop baseline), number of latent tokens and Jacobi iterations, and the role of the last reasoning step.
Efficiency analysis is included (forward-pass counts relative to Full CoT, 62-92% reduction), and the paper is honest that PCCoT results are omitted due to near-identical efficiency.

Interpretability analysis (decoding latent thoughts, teacher-student KV cosine similarity heatmaps) provides qualitative evidence that the student internalizes the teacher's trace, strengthening the mechanistic claims.
Reproducibility appears reasonable: detailed hyperparameters in Appendix C, dataset details, and pseudocode for the eviction score.
weaknesses: Limited scope of evaluation: all experiments are on GSM8k and its augmented/paraphrased variants (GSM8k-Hard, SVAMP as zero-shot). No evaluation beyond grade-school math, so claims about scalability to 'real-world reasoning workloads' and generalization are only partially supported.

Incremental contribution relative to CODI and PCCoT: the method builds directly on the PCCoT/Jacobi framework and CODI self-distillation, adding an R-KV-based eviction plus an L1/MSE KV-matching loss; the technical novelty is a straightforward combination rather than a fundamentally new mechanism.

Results are not uniformly dominant: e.g., on LLaMA3.2-1B GSM8k-Hard, CODI (12.8) edges out KA Va (12.7), and CODI wins some SVAMP cells at 3B, suggesting the advantage over the strongest baseline is modest in places.

Inconsistent hyperparameter choices across models/datasets (L1 for some, MSE for others, varying alpha_2, projection on/off) are tuned per setting, raising concerns about sensitivity and fair comparison effort relative to baselines.

The distillation targets KV entries of the same base model (self-distillation), so the ceiling is bounded by the teacher; the gap to Full CoT remains substantial (e.g., 56.5 vs 61.6 on LLaMA-1B GSM8k), and the paper does not deeply analyze why.

Several baseline numbers are copied from prior work (dagger notation), and some cells are missing (e.g., Coconut/CODI on GSM8k-Aug-NL for LLaMA-1B), which complicates exact comparisons; cross-model hyperparameter transfer for new baselines is only briefly described.

The interpretability claim that KV distillation prevents hard-token correspondence on longer traces (Sec 5.1) is a plausible hypothesis but is supported only by a few qualitative examples, not a systematic study.

strengths: The core idea is sensible and clearly motivated: using a compressed teacher KV-cache as a stepwise supervision signal for latent reasoning addresses a genuine weakness of prior latent-reasoning methods (CODI, Coconut, PCCoT), which supervise only endpoints or single distillation tokens.

The paper is transparent about positioning: it clearly delineates its relationship to R-KV (eviction), CODI (self-distillation), and PCCoT (Jacobi iteration), and ablations (Tables 3-4, Figures 4-6) isolate the contribution of each component.

Evaluation spans three model families (Qwen2.5-0.5B, Llama3.2-1B/3B) and two training datasets (equation-only and natural-language traces), with standard errors over three seeds, zero-shot OOD evaluation (GSM8k-Hard, SVAMP), and efficiency measurements in forward passes.

The interpretability analysis (decoding latent traces, teacher-student KV cosine similarity heatmaps) is a nice touch that goes beyond accuracy tables and lends qualitative support to the claim that the student internalizes the teacher's reasoning.
Hyperparameters, eviction pseudocode, and dataset details are provided in appendices, aiding reproducibility of the training recipe.
weaknesses: Novelty is incremental. The method is essentially CODI's self-distillation setup plus R-KV eviction (a published, off-the-shelf compression method with an official implementation the authors use directly) plus PCCoT's Jacobi decoding. The main technical contribution reduces to matching student K/V to the evicted teacher cache with an L1/MSE loss; each ingredient exists, and the paper does not analyze why KV matching works theoretically or when it should fail.

Empirical gains over the strongest baseline (CODI) are small and inconsistent. On Llama3.2-1B GSM8k-Hard, CODI (12.8) beats KaVA (12.7); on several 3B settings the margins are within ~0.3-1 point, comparable to the reported standard errors. The 'consistently outperforms strong latent baselines' claim is overstated.

The efficiency results largely inherit from PCCoT's Jacobi iteration, not from KaVA's contribution. The authors even skip reporting PCCoT numbers in Table 2 because they 'would be similar to ours,' which makes the efficiency comparison uninformative about the actual novelty.

Hyperparameter choices are erratic and undermine the method's narrative: the KV loss switches between MSE and Smooth L1 depending on the dataset/model, alpha_2 varies (1 vs 2), and r-KV lambda is set to 0.0 for Llama3.2-3B GSM8k-Aug-NL - contradicting the claim that combining importance and redundancy is important (Figure 5). This suggests fragile tuning rather than a robust method.

Scope is narrow: only GSM8k-style arithmetic word problems on 0.5B-3B instruct models, with a large remaining gap to the Full CoT upper bound (e.g., 56.5 vs 61.6 on 1B). No evidence the approach transfers beyond math or to genuinely long natural-language traces, which is where the paper claims its main advantage lies.

The claim of being 'the first to distill from a compressed KV-cache' is a thin framing; KV-MixDistill (cited in the paper) already trains a compressed-cache student, and the delta is the stepwise KV matching rather than a fundamentally new capability.

Some analyses raise unanswered questions: the GSM8k-Aug-NL traces are largely undecodable (Section 5.1), yet the paper provides only a hypothesis for why, and the heatmap evidence (Figures 7-12) is qualitative with no quantitative corroboration.

strengths: The paper addresses a genuinely important gap in latent reasoning: the lack of direct, stepwise supervision for continuous thought tokens. The idea of using a compressed teacher KV-cache as a supervision target is novel and well-motivated, since evicted caches destroy token correspondence and invalidate standard activation-matching distillation.

The method is clearly described and technically sound: the redundancy+importance eviction scoring (adapted from R-KV) is combined sensibly with a direct KV-matching loss, and the training objective cleanly integrates the CODI self-distillation loss with the new KV loss.

Evaluation is reasonably thorough: three model families (Qwen2.5-0.5B, Llama3.2-1B/3B), two training data regimes (equation-only vs. natural-language traces), in-distribution and zero-shot OOD benchmarks, and forward-pass efficiency measurements. The paper consistently outperforms strong latent baselines (CODI, PCCoT, Coconut, iCoT), with the largest gains on the harder natural-language setting, which directly supports the central claim.

Good ablation coverage: the loss type/coefficient sensitivity, eviction method comparison (including a simple truncation baseline), number of latent tokens and Jacobi iterations, and the 'removing last step' experiment that highlights how KV distillation removes reliance on a privileged distillation token.

The interpretability analysis (decoding latent traces, teacher-student KV cosine similarity heatmaps) provides qualitative insight into what the latent tokens learn, strengthening the paper beyond raw accuracy numbers.

Reproducibility appears solid: hyperparameters are fully specified in Appendix C, pseudocode for eviction is provided, datasets are publicly identified, and results are averaged over three seeds with standard errors.
weaknesses: Narrow experimental scope: all experiments are on GSM8k-family math datasets. Given the claim of bridging 'natural-language reasoning traces' with latent reasoning, evaluation on at least one non-math domain (e.g., commonsense or logical reasoning) would substantially strengthen the generality claims.

Novelty is somewhat incremental: the framework is largely a careful combination of existing components — R-KV eviction, CODI self-distillation, and PCCoT-style Jacobi parallel decoding — with the main new element being the direct KV-matching loss against a compressed cache. The paper's 'first to demonstrate' claim is fair, but the technical machinery is mostly assembled from prior work.

A persistent, sizable gap to Full CoT remains (e.g., 56.5 vs. 61.6 on Llama3.2-1B GSM8k), and on some settings (Llama3.2-3B, GSM8k-AUG) CODI is competitive or close. The paper does not deeply analyze when or why KV distillation helps most.

Efficiency is measured only in forward passes; memory footprint, wall-clock latency, and actual KV-cache size at inference are not reported, which matters for the efficiency/deployability claims that motivate the work.

Hyperparameter sensitivity is high: the best loss type (L1 vs. MSE vs. Smooth-L1), layer-wise standardization, and loss coefficients differ across model/dataset combinations (Appendix C), raising concerns about the robustness of the method and the amount of tuning required to reproduce the reported gains.
The interpretability analysis is anecdotal (single-prompt examples); the hypothesis explaining why GSM8k-AUG-NL latent traces do not decode readably is plausible but not rigorously verified.

Only small models (0.5B-3B) and LoRA fine-tuning are tested; 'scales to larger backbones' is a modest scaling claim (1B to 3B) and the interaction with full fine-tuning or larger models is unexplored.

strengths: Novel and well-motivated idea: using a compressed teacher KV-cache (which lacks token correspondence) as a stepwise supervision signal for latent reasoning is a genuinely new direction that addresses the known supervision gap in latent/continuous CoT methods, and is complementary rather than redundant to existing endpoint-level distillation (CODI).

Comprehensive evaluation: three model families (Qwen2.5-0.5B, Llama3.2-1B/3B), three training datasets (GSM8k-Aug, GSM8k-Aug-NL, MetaMathQA), in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks, and comparison against relevant baselines (CODI, PCCoT, iCoT, Coconut) with Full CoT and No-CoT bounds.

Strong empirical results: consistent improvements over all latent baselines across settings, with especially large gains on natural-language traces (GSM8k-Aug-NL), which prior work reports as a weakness of latent reasoning; efficiency results (62-92% fewer forward passes than Full CoT) are clearly reported.

Good ablation coverage: KV loss type/coefficient, eviction method (R-KV vs cosine-only vs attention-only vs cropping), number of latent tokens and Jacobi iterations, dataset scaling, removal of last trace step, and model components (distillation loss, projection layer).

Thoughtful interpretability analysis: decoding latent traces into teacher-equivalent text and cosine-similarity analysis of student-vs-teacher KV correspondence, which supports the mechanistic claim that the student internalizes the compressed cache.
Reproducibility appears solid: full hyperparameter tables, dataset details, pseudocode for the eviction score, and efficiency measurement methodology are provided.
weaknesses: The method is essentially a combination of existing components (CODI self-distillation framework, PCCoT Jacobi decoding, R-KV eviction) with a new KV-matching loss; while the combination is novel and effective, the technical depth of the core contribution is moderate.

Evaluation is restricted to small models (<=3B) and math word-problem tasks; claims of scalability to 'larger backbones' and general reasoning are not tested at a scale or domain (e.g., code, logic, science) that would establish broader significance.

Hyperparameters are highly per-dataset and per-model (e.g., KV loss switches between L1/MSE/Smooth-L1, layer-wise normalization and projection toggled, alpha_1=0 on MetaMathQA), which weakens the robustness of the results and suggests the method requires nontrivial tuning; the ablation showing different best losses across datasets is a stability concern.

Large accuracy gap remains to Full CoT (e.g., 65.7 vs 73.2 on 3B), and in some cells gains over the second-best baseline are within or near one standard error (e.g., GSM8k-Hard and SVAMP for Llama-1b), so the claim of 'consistently outperforms' is somewhat stronger than the evidence in a few settings.

Interpretability findings are anecdotal (single-prompt decodings) and the explanation for why GSM8k-Aug-NL latent traces resist read-out is only a hypothesis; a quantitative interpretability analysis would strengthen Section 5.
Baselines other than KaVa appear to use fixed hyperparameters, while KaVa's hyperparameters are swept per dataset/model, raising a potential fairness concern in the comparisons.

strengths: The core idea is interesting and reasonably novel: using a compressed teacher KV-cache as a stepwise supervision target for latent reasoning, sidestepping the ill-posed token-correspondence problem after head/layer-wise eviction. This is a sensible and distinct position relative to endpoint-supervision methods like CODI.

Empirical evaluation is fairly comprehensive: three model families (Qwen2.5-0.5B, Llama3.2-1B/3B), multiple training datasets (GSM8k-AUG, GSM8k-AUG-NL, MetaMathQA), in-distribution and out-of-distribution test sets, efficiency measurements, and accuracy-efficiency Pareto analyses.

Consistent improvements over strong latent baselines (CODI, PCCoT, Coconut, iCoT), with particularly notable gains in the more challenging natural-language and longer-trace settings (e.g., +5-10 points over CODI on GSM8k-Aug-NL), supporting the claim that KV distillation helps precisely where latent reasoning previously struggled.

Good ablation coverage: loss type/coefficient, eviction method (importance vs. redundancy vs. cropping), number of latent tokens and Jacobi iterations, data scaling, and removal of the last reasoning step. The ablation showing KV distillation compensates for the removal of the CODI distillation token is a meaningful validation.

The interpretability section (decoded latent traces, teacher-student KV cosine similarity heatmaps) provides qualitative insight into what the latent tokens learn and why hard-token readout fails on natural-language traces.
weaknesses: The method is largely incremental: it is CODI/PCCoT plus one additional Lp-matching loss (Eq. 7) applied to KV entries, with the eviction mechanism borrowed essentially unchanged from R-KV. The technical machinery is simple, and the 'first to demonstrate' framing oversells a modest delta over Shen et al. (2025) and Wu et al. (2025).

A key technical assumption is under-specified: Eq. 7 performs element-wise matching between the student's M latent K/V entries and the compressed teacher cache, but eviction is done independently per layer and head with no explicit ordering or correspondence mechanism between the surviving teacher KV entries and the student's latent steps. The paper should clarify whether (and how) positional alignment is enforced; if it is not, the loss only encourages set-level matching, which weakens the 'stepwise supervision' narrative.

Scope is narrow: all experiments are arithmetic/math word problems (GSM8k, MetaMathQA and derivatives). No logic, code, or general reasoning benchmarks, making generalization claims about 'latent reasoning' hard to assess.

Some empirical gains are small and within reported standard errors (e.g., GSM8k-Hard 12.7 vs 12.9 for Llama-1B), and on several settings KaVa approaches but does not approach the Full-CoT upper bound consistently; significance testing beyond 3-seed standard errors is absent.

Fairness and consistency concerns: hyperparameters (loss type, alpha coefficients, projection on/off, lambda) vary per dataset/model and were tuned on validation, while some baselines use copied or partially re-tuned settings; KaVa itself changes configuration across settings (e.g., alpha_1 = 0 in MetaMathQA/hybrid experiments), making it unclear whether the comparison isolates the KV loss or general tuning advantages.

Efficiency gains largely stem from the PCCoT Jacobi machinery rather than the KV-distillation contribution itself; KaVa/PCCoT are grouped in Table 2, so the paper's own efficiency contribution is not cleanly isolated.

Fixed latent budget (M=24) and no direct empirical comparison against closely related distillation approaches such as KV-Distill (Chari et al., 2025) or SoftCoT; the related-work distinction is textual rather than experimental.
No explicit code release is stated, limiting reproducibility despite detailed hyperparameter tables.

strengths: The core idea is genuinely novel and well-motivated: using a teacher's compressed KV-cache (whose per-layer, per-head eviction destroys token correspondence) as a stepwise supervision signal for a latent-reasoning student is a clever bridge between two previously separate research threads (KV-cache compression and latent/continuous CoT reasoning).

The method is technically well-specified: the combined redundancy–importance eviction score (Eq. 4–6), the KV-matching loss (Eq. 7), handling of padding tokens and GQA, and pseudocode in App. A make the approach reproducible; hyperparameters are fully reported.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: three model families/sizes (Qwen-0.5B, Llama-1B, Llama-3B), two trace styles (equation-only vs natural language), MetaMathQA scaling experiments with an accuracy–efficiency Pareto analysis, OOD benchmarks, and direct comparisons against CODI, PCCoT, iCoT, and Coconut with several seeds and standard errors.

Good ablation coverage: distillation loss vs projection layer, removal of the last teacher step, loss type/coefficient sensitivity, eviction-method ablation (R-KV vs cosine-only vs attention-only vs cropping), number of latent tokens/iterations, and dataset-size scaling.

The interpretability analysis (decoding latent traces, cosine-similarity heatmaps between student latent KV and teacher full/evicted KV) provides qualitative evidence that the distillation objective does what it claims, and is honestly presented (e.g., acknowledging the NL dataset resists decoding).
The paper is candid about limitations, e.g., setting α1=0 for stability on MetaMathQA and that data scaling matters, which increases credibility.
weaknesses: Scope is narrow: all experiments are on grade-school arithmetic (GSM8k variants, MetaMathQA, SVAMP, multiArith). No evidence on harder reasoning (MATH beyond MATH500, code, logic), so the claim that this 'establishes compressed KV-cache distillation as a scalable supervision signal for latent reasoning' is stronger than the evidence.

Gains over the strongest baseline (CODI) are often modest and inconsistent across settings; e.g., on Llama-3B with GSM8k-Aug-NL, CODI beats KaVa on SVAMP (70.1 vs 66.1), and on Llama-1B GSM8k-Aug SVAMP CODI is competitive. The headline advantage is mainly on the NL datasets and Qwen-0.5B.

The alignment between the (unordered) top-M evicted teacher KV pairs and the student's ordered latent steps is not formally analyzed: the KV-matching loss pairs index i of the evicted cache with latent step i, but eviction is per-layer/per-head independent selection, so the semantics of this index alignment (and its sensitivity to ordering) deserve more discussion or an ablation.

Heavy reliance on prior components: the framework combines CODI's self-distillation objective, PCCoT's Jacobi decoding, and R-KV eviction; the contribution is the KV-matching loss on top. This is fine but positions the paper more as an incremental-but-effective addition than a fundamentally new technique.

Efficiency is measured only in forward passes; wall-clock latency, memory footprint at inference, and comparison to simply compressing the full CoT cache at inference time (a natural competing efficiency strategy) are not reported.

Hyperparameter choices appear somewhat inconsistent across models/datasets (e.g., r-kv λ=0.0 for Llama-3B NL, different loss types per dataset), which raises mild concerns about tuning fairness relative to baselines and about method robustness, even though a sweep protocol is described.
Standard error is reported only for some configurations (mainly Llama-1B); several Table 1 results (Qwen-0.5B baselines, Llama-3B) lack error bars, weakening statistical comparison.
